entities.summary: Reiner Schürmann was a German philosopher. He was a professor of Philosophy at The New School for Social Research in New York City from 1975 to his death. He wrote all his major published work in French. Deeply influenced by Heidegger, Meister Eckhart, and contemporary continental thought, Schürmann developed a radical critique of metaphysical and political first principles culminating in analyses of broken hegemonies, singularity, and non-foundational praxis. In recent years, his work have been increasingly translated and discussed in different countries like Italy or Mexico; in 2025, an anthology remarked that academic interest in Schürmann's philosophical work had grown notably.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Reiner Schürmann's philosophical work has had a notable impact on contemporary continental thought, particularly in Italy and Mexico, where his ideas have been increasingly translated and discussed. His analyses of broken hegemonies and non-foundational praxis have contributed to a growing interest in radical critiques of metaphysical and political first principles.
